runtime.name: omp
runtime.configuration: Generated interrogate Skill and reviewer/synthesizer roles copied into a disposable Git fixture; empty Skill allowlist; asynchronous task support enabled.
runtime.permissionProfile: read-only workflow contract in a disposable repository with auto-approved inspection commands

assertions.evidence: The root explicitly loaded the generated interrogate Skill and its packaged references.
The final verdict retained the exact intent, project/lib/window.mjs, Git revision, and SHA-256 80bf5704a0bcc57ee05b4143aea6b5bc258c45bf3c7a4d1a2264829cfcf99669.
ReviewerA and ReviewerB were both started before the runtime waited for either result.
Both reviewers received the same frozen intent, source, hash, rubric, quality lens, and output contract.
Both complete attributable results were collected without follow-up, retry, replacement, or rewriting.
Synthesizer1 was created only after both reviewer results froze and received those frozen results.
The verdict mapped each finding to ReviewerA, ReviewerB, or both and preserved the lone ReviewerB observation.
The root executed examples confirming missing lower-bound rejection, upper-bound clamping, and partial numeric parsing.
Runtime model_change and resolvedModel metadata showed cursor/default for both reviewers and the synthesizer; the verdict explicitly stated diversity was not established.
Outer git status was clean and the reviewed file retained its frozen SHA-256.

limitations: All three child sessions resolved to the same runtime model, so this proves independent sessions but not model diversity.
OMP delivery remains D0 overall because the separate plugin-manager D1 gate is unresolved.
